html:
Samarkand is a city in the Zeravshan valley of what is now Uzbekistan, one of the oldest cities of Central Asia and a great stop on the Silk Road.

As Maracanda it was the chief city of Sogdia, whose merchants carried trade between China, India and Persia. Alexander the Great took it in 329 BCE. Arab armies conquered it in the early 700s and it became a Muslim city. Tradition says Chinese prisoners taken in 751 taught papermaking there. Under the Samanids it and Bukhara grew rich on trade, and later it was ruled by the Kara-Khanids and the Khwarazmshahs.

Genghis Khan's army sacked it in 1220. Timur made it his capital from 1370 and filled it with buildings, raised by craftsmen taken from the cities he conquered: the Bibi-Khanym mosque and his own tomb, the Gur-e-Amir. His grandson Ulugh Beg built an observatory and a madrasa on the Registan square.

Later it passed to the Uzbek khanates. Russia took it in 1868, and the Trans-Caspian Railway reached it in 1888. Its old centre is now a World Heritage Site.
sum: Samarkand is a city in the Zeravshan valley of what is now Uzbekistan, one of the oldest cities of Central Asia and a great stop on the Silk Road.
